findings.title: Orphaned main menu and tagline washed out by the sun glare
findings.where: Title screen: wordmark and tagline centred mid-frame, two-item menu box in the bottom-left corner, 'Arcade' chip top-left
findings.problem: The teal SMDUEL wordmark sits directly over the brightest part of the sun/dust haze with no scrim or outline, and the small white tagline under it is laid across that same bright band so its right half nearly disappears into the sky. Meanwhile the only actionable element — a small rounded slate panel with 'New Driver' / 'Controls' — is jammed into the bottom-left corner, leaving the whole centre-bottom of the frame empty and the centre-right of the lockup unreadable.
findings.why: This is the first frame of the game. The eye lands on the logo and then hunts for 'Press Start', finds only a corner box, and reads the layout as broken or missing. Copy that can't be read in half a second is wasted, and low-contrast type over a bright sky makes the screen look like a wallpaper with UI pasted on top.
findings.fix: Add a soft radial black scrim (roughly 45% opacity, ~420px tall) behind the wordmark + tagline lockup and give both a 1px dark outline / 2px drop shadow so they separate from the sky. Then move the menu directly under the tagline, centre-aligned, as 2–3 full-width rows (~32px type, 420px wide) with the selected row filled teal and a left chevron marker; keep the top-left 'Arcade' chip only if it is a genuine global toggle, otherwise remove it from this screen.

findings.title: The hub city is gray-box: untextured building blocks, no shadows, no streets
findings.where: Open-world city frame (New York hub): the whole playfield — buildings, plaza floor, circular wall, and the green/orange/cyan chevrons above buildings
findings.problem: Buildings are small flat grey cubes with near-identical pixel noise, no cast shadows, no roof or silhouette variation, floating on one continuous cracked-tile ground plane that shows no streets, kerbs or block layout — the circular wall is the only structure with any real silhouette. The colour chevrons marking Fight/Build/Care/Jobs sit above buildings and are clipped by the top edge of the frame, and several buildings are cropped away entirely.
findings.why: This is where the player lives between runs, and right now it reads as a debug/gray-box level rather than one of 'sixteen cities', which destroys the world-building promise immediately. With no streets or lighting the player can't tell where they can drive or which building is which, and clipped markers mean destinations can be missed completely.
findings.fix: Give every building a 2–3 tile offset shadow blob in one fixed light direction plus a distinct roof shape and trim tint per type (Fight red, Build amber, Care green, Jobs cyan — matching the existing bottom-right legend), and paint real streets: darker asphalt strips with light kerb lines radiating from the plaza to the gate so drivable lanes are obvious. Separately, clamp or bias the camera in the hub (shift the target toward the building cluster or pull back ~15%) so building tops and their chevrons never leave the frame.

findings.title: No sense of speed: tiny car, dead-centre framing, no motion reference
findings.where: Road and practice arena frames: the player car is a small speck dead-centre, surrounded by an unbroken mottled floor texture
findings.problem: The driving camera is pulled out so far the vehicle occupies roughly 8% of the frame width, pinned to the exact centre of a huge, featureless pixel-noise ground plane — no lane paint in the arena, no skid marks, no dust, no props, no drop shadow under the car. Nothing in the frame moves or flows past the player.
findings.why: At highway speed this reads as a parked car on a placeholder floor: no peripheral motion, no landmark flow, no sense of travelling anywhere, and combat suffers because the car and its weapons are too small to read at a glance. It is the single biggest reason the game looks unfinished in motion.
findings.fix: Zoom the driving camera in ~1.5x (car at ~15–18% of frame width) with an 80–120px lookahead offset in the direction of travel and a mild speed-based zoom-out so fast driving stays playable. Add motion cues to the ground: persistent skid/dust decals where tyres scrub, painted white edge lines and yellow lane dashes on the arena floor (matching the road's existing paint), scattered debris/props, and a soft dark drop shadow under the car.

findings.title: Radar is a blank black disc and reads as broken
findings.where: Bottom-left RADAR panel on the road and practice arena frames
findings.problem: The instrument is a near-black circle with one faint dark-green wedge and a tiny cyan arrow for the player, plus a caption reading 'Orientation: north-up'. There are no range rings, no heading ticks, no contacts, no world features — just a void with a hair-thin crosshair.
findings.why: A combat HUD instrument that shows nothing looks unimplemented or frozen; the player will assume the feature is broken and gets zero early warning about off-screen threats, which is exactly what a radar is for in a highway-survival game.
findings.fix: Render three concentric range rings with heading ticks every 30°, animate the sweep wedge with a gradient that leaves a ~1s fading trail, plot contacts as coloured blips (red hostile, yellow neutral, cyan objective) whose size scales with distance, and draw the road/arena edge as thin grey arcs so the radar is never empty. When there genuinely are no contacts, show an explicit 'NO CONTACTS' label instead of a black void.

findings.title: Armor readout uses unreadable bracket glyphs
findings.where: Top-right CONDITION panel on the road and arena frames: the ARMOUR rows (FRONT / REAR / LEFT / RIGHT / UNDERBODY)
findings.problem: Each facing is rendered as tiny ASCII-style bracket glyphs — '|:--:|', '[ ]:--:[ ]' — at roughly 9px in the same grey-on-grey as the row labels, with no bar fill and no colour coding. The underbody row is pure punctuation. The tyre and plant rows below it use a different green-dot-plus-bar language again.
findings.why: Armor state is what you glance at mid-fight while dodging; if it takes two seconds to decode, players will misread it or stop looking, and the whole panel reads as leftover debug text rather than a real instrument, undermining trust in the HUD.
findings.fix: Replace each armor facing with a 5-segment horizontal bar (~60px wide) filled green → amber → red and the numeric value (e.g. '6/8') at the right end; give underbody the same treatment on its own full-width row. Convert the tyre, plant and driver rows to that same segmented-bar language so the panel uses one consistent visual system.
